## Week of 2026-11-12

> Generated by `podcast-recommender` scheduled task. Episode dates below come from third-party podcast directories, so check the feeds for exact titles.

### Scam Inc (The Economist)
Host: Sue-Lin Wong
Why for Fred: His last month of listening has been almost all serialised investigations (Kill List, Wisecrack, Aftermath, Where Is Austin Tice?, The Conti Files). Scam Inc is the same format applied to finance and crypto: an eight-part series on the industrial "pig-butchering" scam economy run from Southeast Asian compounds, including how stolen money is laundered through crypto rails. It won a Peabody Award (the Peabody site lists it as a 2025 winner). It's a finished 2025 series, so it's a binge rather than a weekly show, and some episodes may sit behind Economist Podcasts+.
Format: Serialised investigative documentary, 8 episodes, ~35–45 min each
Sample episode to start with: Episode 1, "The bottom line" (Feb 2025); it's serialised, so start at the beginning
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1785226676) · [Acast](https://shows.acast.com/scam-inc/about)

---

### Complex Systems with Patrick McKenzie (patio11)
Host: Patrick McKenzie (ex-Stripe; writes *Bits about Money*)
Why for Fred: McKenzie explains how financial plumbing really works: payments finality, brokerage transfers, revenue recognition, fraud. That's the infrastructure underneath both the equities and DeFi sides of Fred's interests, and it's a close neighbour of Odd Lots and Money Stuff. He also covers AI in practice, with episodes on Claude Code and on what LLMs can and can't do for writers, which touches Fred's AI-at-work and writing threads.
Format: Interview plus solo essay readings, weekly (Thursdays), ~30–75 min
Sample episode to start with: "How brokerage transfers actually work" (Jun 2026) or "The $900 million wire that wasn't final" (Oct 2026)
Links: [complexsystemspodcast.com](https://www.complexsystemspodcast.com) · [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/complex-systems-with-patrick-mckenzie-patio11/id1753399812)

---

### Planet MicroCap Podcast
Host: Robert Kraft
Why for Fred: Nearly 500 episodes of interviews with microcap fund managers and private investors on how they source and underwrite ideas in under-followed stocks. That's the small-cap end of the market podcast-pender-fund works in. It has a real European strand: "Europe's Hidden Gems" with Thomas Richard (Philippe Hottinguer Gestion, Paris) and "Deep Value in Europe" with Iggy on Investing on activism and value traps. Caveat: the newest episode I could confirm was #496 (June 2026), so check the feed is still active.
Format: Long-form interview, roughly weekly, ~45–60 min
Sample episode to start with: "Deep Value in Europe, Shareholder Activism, Stag Hunts, and Value Traps with Iggy on Investing"
Links: [planetmicrocap.podbean.com](https://planetmicrocap.podbean.com) · [Pocket Casts](https://pocketcasts.com/podcasts/b7da5730-1767-0133-2593-059c869cc4eb)

---

### The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck
Host: Matt Turck (FirstMark Capital)
Why for Fred: This is the most inference-focused of the AI shows suggested so far. 2026 episodes include Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman on why inference is now the bottleneck, OpenAI's Sachin Katti on compute supply ("We Can't Build Fast Enough"), Stephen Balaban on the neocloud boom, and Dylan Patel on Nvidia's moat. It picks up directly from the Dwarkesh compute-prices episode and the Gavin Baker "AI Market Jitters" episode Fred finished, with Turck asking from a VC's point of view.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~60–90 min
Sample episode to start with: Andrew Feldman (Cerebras) on inference speed (Jul 2026), or Sebastian Raschka's "State of LLMs 2026" (Jan 2026)
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id1686238724) · [mattturck.com](https://mattturck.com)

runs.content:
## Week of 2026-11-05

> Generated by `podcast-recommender` scheduled task. Three picks this week: a fourth option, People I (Mostly) Admire, was dropped because Steve Levitt ended the show around Dec 2025–Jan 2026.

### Cheeky Pint
Host: John Collison (Stripe co-founder and president)
Why for Fred: Collison interviews the CEOs who are building enterprise and consumer AI. Recent guests include Sundar Pichai on Google's AI history, ElevenLabs' Mati Staniszewski on voice AI and Evan Spiegel on what comes after smartphones. He's an operator talking to operators, so the episodes are about unit economics and strategy rather than hype. That suits Fred's interest in enterprise AI and inference trends, and it complements Dwarkesh, which is more research-led, and Ed Zitron, who is sceptical. The voice-AI episode also bears on Lightfin's audio production.
Format: Long-form conversation, roughly weekly, ~45–75 min
Sample episode to start with: Mati Staniszewski (ElevenLabs) on voice AI (Apr 2026), or Sundar Pichai on Google's AI history (Apr 2026)
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/id1821055332) · [RSS feed](https://feeds.transistor.fm/cheeky-pint-with-john-collison)

---

### The Doctor's Kitchen Podcast
Host: Dr Rupy Aujla (UK NHS GP)
Why for Fred: This is a UK-based, evidence-led show where a practising GP interviews researchers. It has a deep run of episodes on brain health and dementia prevention, which is one of Fred's stated health priorities. Examples are neurophysiologist Louisa Nicola on creatine, omega-3 and exercise for protecting the brain, and a neurologist on metabolic health and the brain. The creatine episode follows on from the Darren Candow Diary of a CEO episode Fred finished. Earlier health picks were mostly US longevity shows (Attia, Patrick, ZOE, Simon Hill), and this one is more practical and focused on food and daily habits.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~1–2 hr (plus short "Snacksize" episodes)
Sample episode to start with: "7 habits a neuroscientist swears by to keep your mind sharp at any age" with Dr Tommy Wood (Mar 2026), then the Dr Louisa Nicola episode on creatine and omega-3 for the brain
Links: [thedoctorskitchen.com/podcasts](https://www.thedoctorskitchen.com/podcasts) · [TuneIn](https://tunein.com/podcasts/p1088217)

---

### Masters in Business (Bloomberg)
Host: Barry Ritholtz (Ritholtz Wealth Management; author of *How Not to Invest*)
Why for Fred: It has more than 10 years of hour-long career-history interviews with allocators, value managers and behavioural-finance academics, over 500 episodes. Ritholtz asks about process and mistakes, not current stock picks, which fits Fred's Buffett/MOI approach. Recent guests line up with his AI and behavioural interests: Glen Kacher on investing in the AI boom (Sep 2026) and Omar Aguilar on decision science in investing (Oct 2026). It's a natural next listen after Invest Like the Best and Capital Allocators.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~60–90 min
Sample episode to start with: "Using Decision Science in Investing" with Omar Aguilar (2 Oct 2026), or "Investing for the AI Boom" with Glen Kacher (18 Sep 2026)
Links: [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/podcast/id730188152) · [Bloomberg / iHeart](https://www.iheart.com/podcast/from-podnews-30972801)
